measurementEvidence.units: source pixels; joint centres estimated under loose cloth
measurementEvidence.torsoDefinition: neck-base to hip; crown-to-hip is 3.59 HU, not the spine segment length

depth.note: No profile/back reference. Preserve volume and validate meaningful orbits; do not claim measured depth.

definitionOfDone: Full-height pose matches the raised right hand and low left hand; long-limbed 8.57 HU proportions remain recognizable.
Green open robe, purple sash/tails, ribbed haramaki and three separate swords match the admitted reference.
Closed left eye/scar, grin, three earrings and short green scalp silhouette survive a head close-up.
Front, +/-35, side, rear-three-quarter, rear and both head views show continuous volumes and attached accessories.
Unobserved side/back are explicitly inferred. No source mesh, Blender model or GLB geometry enters the factory.

featureGroups.name: Overall silhouette and proportions
qualityCriteria: Bounding shape, dominant curves, negative spaces, and scale relationships are explicitly described.
failureModes: model reads as a generic placeholder instead of the reference object
major proportions are guessed without evidence

featureGroups.name: Primary structure and hierarchy
qualityCriteria: Major parts, joints, seams, contact points, and parent-child relationships are named before code generation.
failureModes: large visible parts are merged into one mesh
component hierarchy is too shallow for the observed complexity

featureGroups.name: Attachment and joint correctness
qualityCriteria: Every visible child appendage, branch, limb, handle, connector, tube, cable, horn, wing, leg, or hinged part has an attachment contract with parent socket, localStart/localEnd, contact type, embed/overlap, and gap tolerance.
failureModes: child part root floats away from the parent
branch/limb/tube is centered in space instead of pivoting from its root
parent-child transform mixes world and local coordinates

featureGroups.name: Surface material response
qualityCriteria: Albedo zones, roughness, normal/bump/displacement intent, cavity dirt, edge wear, and local overrides are specified where visible.
Important materials define independent albedo, roughness, height/normal, and AO responses instead of reusing one texture for unrelated PBR channels.
Surface response is decomposed into macro, meso, and micro frequency bands with scale and amplitude tied to object scale.
failureModes: local material variation is missing or not tied to image evidence

featureGroups.name: Reference color, material, and lighting response
qualityCriteria: Material-pass names the reference-derived albedo palette, roughness variation, tactile normal/bump/displacement response, and local masks.
When a source image is available, run reference PBR extraction and require confidence >= 0.7 before treating maps as implementation-ready.
Lighting-pass names key/fill/rim or environment light, exposure, tone mapping, background, and contact shadow behavior.
Neutral, grazing-angle, and reference-matched renders prove that surface relief survives relighting and is not painted into albedo.
failureModes: model has acceptable shape but reads as flat shaded or plastic
colors are a generic average instead of reference-observed local color zones
lighting is evenly ambient and cannot reproduce the source value range

visualDeltaChecks: local feature placement and scale delta
antiShallowSpecRules: Do not proceed to code if qualityContract.qualityBar is unassessed.
Do not proceed to code if the spec only contains a root component for a moderate or complex object.
Do not proceed to code if required featureGroups are not represented by componentTree, materials, or repetitionSystems.
Do not proceed to code if visible local features are described only in prose and not attached to components/materials/evidenceRefs.
Do not proceed past structural-pass if attached child parts lack attachment.parentSocket, localStart, localEnd, embedDepth/overlap, and gapTolerance.
Do not pass material look-dev when albedo is reused as roughness, height, normal, or AO.
Do not pass material look-dev without macro, meso, and micro surface frequency bands for close-up materials.
Do not pass reference-fidelity material look-dev from a source image without usable referencePbr maps or an explicit documented limitation.
Do not patch a spec with extracted PBR maps when extraction confidence is below the target threshold unless the user explicitly accepts lower fidelity.
Do not place adjacent separate-geometry parts below 0.02 world-unit seam overlap (source: grimoire/build/geometry_patterns.md).
Do not satisfy raised or recessed relief, fasteners, or grip structure with a map alone when the feature affects form; use geometry or displacement (source: grimoire/build/geometry_patterns.md).

mustMatch: reference-derived PBR material response at or above 0.7 confidence when source pixels are usable
niceToHave: micro scratches, stains, chips, and dirt masks

visualAcceptance.scoringRule: AI vision must inspect a side-by-side reference/render sheet and score the current pass from 0 to 1. Pixel-diff code may assist diagnostics but cannot approve a pass.

featureReviewPolicy.selectionRule: Choose only the most visually salient, identity-defining, user-prioritized, or high-risk semantic systems. Group repeated parts instead of reviewing every mesh. AI vision scores every selected feature from the same full reference/render pair.

specRefineTriggers: local feature not traceable to viewEvidence
codeRefineTriggers: spec is adequate but generated geometry/material does not match
lighting hides geometry or material response
stopCriteria: target fidelity reached or user accepts current approximation
remaining gaps require new reference images or manual art

screenshotPolicy.minimumEvidence: Each visual pass needs a reference image, rendered screenshot, side-by-side comparison sheet, AI vision score, layer scores, and critique before choosing continue.
screenshotPolicy.reviewPairRule: Compare the same camera/viewpoint whenever possible; do not judge a front reference against a random render angle.
screenshotPolicy.acceptanceAuthority: AI vision review of the comparison sheet. Code-generated pixel similarity is not sufficient evidence.

featureReviewTargets.name: Source head units and long robe proportions
Bent raised right arm and three sword placements
Curved lapels join a continuous back, neck and torso
Five-digit grips and separate sword assemblies retain contact
Closed left eye/scar, narrow open eye and grin

nextRequiredEvidence: All observed major parts remain attached from meaningful orbit views.
no floating child roots/joints in the browser screenshot
browser render screenshot from your agent's browser/screenshot tool
side-by-side reference/render comparison sheet for AI vision review
banded interior difference vs the reference baseline (forge/stage4_review/interior_difference.py --from/--to per region)
scalp exposure below the hard maximum, measured on geometry before rendering (forge/stage4_review/scalp_exposure.py)
hair gate comparing banded coverage, hairline offset and highlight-band position against the reference (forge/stage4_review/hair_gate.py)
AI vision score at or above the visual acceptance threshold
all critical semantic feature scores from the shared image pair at or above their thresholds
self-correction review appended with action=continue before the next pass

referencePbrExtraction.acceptedLimitation: single-image extraction is reference-derived inference, not exact photogrammetry

mustAvoid: plastic-looking smooth bark, stone, cloth, foliage, or aged material
local color/detail described only in prose without material masks
claiming exact PBR recovery when confidence is below the target threshold
reference lighting copied without separating material readability

screenshotReview: Compare albedo palette and local color zones.
Compare cavity dirt, edge wear, stains, moss, scratches, or other local masks.
Compare key/fill/rim structure, exposure, tone mapping, background, and contact shadows.
Capture a neutral-light render to verify material readability without reference lighting.
Capture a grazing-light close-up to expose flat normals, uniform roughness, tiling, and plastic highlights.
Capture a reference-matched render from the same camera framing as the source.

actionReadiness.contract: Every macro/meso component should be generated as a stable named Object3D pivot node with a mesh child, action metadata, optional sockets, collider proxy, and destruction metadata.
requiredComponentFields: attachment for child appendages, connectors, limbs, tubes, handles, legs, horns, wings, branches, or cables
authoringRules: Do not collapse independently movable parts into one mesh.
Put transforms on component pivot groups, not only on raw meshes.
For attached child parts, put the pivot at the semantic root/socket and build visible geometry from localStart to localEnd.
Represent hinge, socket, detachable, and breakable intent even when no animation is implemented yet.
Use simplified collider proxies for runtime physics instead of visual mesh colliders by default.

destructionPolicy.fractureGroupNaming: Use stable semantic names such as body-shell, left-hinge, glass-panel, branch-segment.
destructionPolicy.debrisStrategy: Prefer detachable component groups and a small number of procedural fragments over random mesh explosion.

assumptions: Side/back depth is inferred, confidence 0.4; no hidden-side fidelity claim.
Static sculpture with clickable parts; no animation readiness claim.
Projection descriptor is a plan; actual projection must be rendered and reviewed before acceptance.

featureReviews.notes: For blockout: long-limbed head-unit scale, robe height and separated boot stance closely follow the fixed full-body pair. Neck-to-head connection and garment structure need the structural pass.
Raised bent right arm, lowered left grip, curved drawn blade and three distinct scabbard endpoints now follow the reference. Hand shape, hilt details and folds remain coarse.

visualEvidence.aiVisionNotes: Scored against the blockout silhouette/proportion goal only. Full appearance remains a rough untextured sculpture. Side view confirms actual head/cloth/boot/blade volumes. Lapels read as flat panels and the neck connection, face, grip anatomy and hair styling must be corrected in later unlocked passes; no final-realism claim.

featureReviews.notes: Proportion-lock only: emitted head-unit ratio 8.5857 vs source 8.57 (0.18% relative delta); full fixed pair confirms robe length and separated boot stance. Surface anatomy and facial likeness remain unfinished.
Fixed full-body pair and meaningful orbit confirm raised elbow and drawn sword pose at macro scale. Gripping fingers and fitted garment structure remain the next pass.

visualEvidence.aiVisionNotes: Inspected full comparison, top (long-axis) and right (thickness-axis) screenshots. Proportion objective is met, measured geometry head units 8.5857 and silhouette IoU .8977. Model still has flat lapels, mitten hands, crown-like hair and unfinished face/materials. Continue specifically to garment/held-prop structure, not final delivery.

Front and right views show curved lapels with a real back and five gripping digits. Self-intersection fails 42/65 sampled vertices on hands. Repetition system lacks elementComponentIds and creates an extra flesh object at origin. Fix spec spacing/union scale and realized repetition membership; no continuation.

Front pair shows jacket panels bending around the torso and both hands overlapping their sword grips. The five separate finger tubes have inward sidewall triangles and fail the actual ray-parity self-intersection gate. Fix winding. The face and crown-shaped hair remain unfinished.

featureReviews.notes: The fitted jacket now has a real back half and curved front panels, but the shoulder silhouette and edge shaping remain crude.
Raised and lowered hands now show several curled skin digits around the handles from front view. Contact remains rough and the structural pass ray-parity has two flagged index-finger samples.

visualEvidence.aiVisionNotes: Inspected fixed front comparison and actual top/right/three-quarter screenshots. The rounded jacket back and fitted lapel surfaces are substantially improved, and fingers are visible around both sword handles. Overall likeness stays low because the head is generic, hair reads as a crown, robe folds are absent and cel-painted details/materials have not been projected. The critical held-sword structural review remains below threshold (.76). Deterministic self-intersection flags one sample on each index finger; fix tube curvature/mesh sampling, recapture and rerun the checks before considering this pass.

featureReviews.notes: Curved lapels and a back shell are visible; garment edges remain coarse.
Five fingers wrap both handles in the front view. One sampled normal vertex on each index-finger tube points slightly inward; ray parity remains blocked.

visualEvidence.aiVisionNotes: Inspected current fixed front, side and overhead captures. The fingers wrap both sword grips and the jacket has a curved open front. The one sample on each index tube is at a curved segment; the mesh resolves cleanly, but averaged face normals offset those points into the winding radius under the parity test. Keep this pass open until it passes. Overall face, hair and surface materials still need substantial work.

featureReviews.notes: Curved lapels and a back shell are visible; garment edges remain coarse.

The deterministically identified samples are mid-curve positions on both index-finger tubes. Analytic normals and finer tessellation did not fix them, so alter the index paths to a smoother, less tightly curved grip and run the full mesh test again.

featureReviews.notes: Curved lapels and back shell remain; contour edges are still coarse.

featureReviews.notes: Open jacket and curved lapels are present, but the broad faceted panels, missing folds, and unfinished edges do not match the reference garment.

visualEvidence.aiVisionNotes: Silhouette, pose and three sword locations are broadly recognizable, but identity and surface fidelity remain weak. The spiky hair collapses into an evenly spaced crown; the face is generic with oversized blank eyes and a cylindrical grin; the layered coat and long robe are smooth, angular masses; the sash has no cloth folds; and fingers plus sword fittings remain blocky. Structural geometry checks passing does not make this a visual-quality pass. Keep the structural pass open.

Rebase the cranial axis to the crown centre while preserving world-space geometry, fit the curved blade outline, and correct the upper skirt centre from measured rows. No AI acceptance or threshold change.

Silhouette IoU now 0.8636, but no pass: the curved blade begins below its guard, is disconnected in projection, and the largest-component bbox fails aspect/scale. Add the actual continuous tang-to-blade bridge. Hair has zero pre-offset self-intersections but 95 after independent standProud pushes: preserve the shell wall with a coherent scalp-distance offset before the mandatory standProud check. No Tier 2 review.

projectedTextureBake.status: descriptor-only; no pixels are baked or rasterized by this script

camera.method: heuristic default-guess camera, not solved from image content; image dimensions give an exact aspect ratio, everything else is a starting point for agent refinement

fovDegrees.rationale: default guess for a portrait-oriented photo (typical phone/short-tele framing)

orientation.note: 0/0/0 assumes a straight-on, level shot; adjust by eye against the reference image.

position.note: Position hint assumes the subject is centered at the origin and the camera looks down -Z.

limitations: no true camera calibration is performed; focal length/FOV/orientation are not recovered from pixels
fovDegrees is a genre default, not a measurement; wrong FOV distorts perceived proportions under overlay
orientation and position are placeholders and will almost always need manual/agent adjustment
this script cannot detect lens distortion, perspective foreshortening, or non-zero roll
camera.note: Final camera match must be confirmed by overlay review: render the fitted mesh from this camera, place it beside or over the reference image, and adjust fovDegrees/orientation/position until silhouette and landmark alignment match before trusting projected texture bakes.

unseenRegionStrategy.note: Regions the reference camera never saw (back, occluded folds, underside) are inferred, not observed.

projectedTextureBake.runtimeApproach: actual projective texturing and UV bake happen in the Three.js runtime via a projective ShaderMaterial (the three-projected-material approach) or an equivalent camera-space projection shader; this descriptor only records the plan for that step
bakeSteps: load the fitted mesh identified by targetMeshId and its UV layout
load sourceImages.delit if present, otherwise sourceImages.reference, as the projection source texture
construct a projection camera in the Three.js scene from the camera block (fovDegrees, aspect, orientation, position)
apply orthographic-front-projection to project the source texture onto mesh surfaces facing the projection camera within tolerance
for surfaces outside the camera's view frustum or facing away, apply the 'palette-continue' strategy
rasterize the resulting camera-space projection into a 1024x1024 UV-space texture
flag any UV texels that received no projected sample (fully unseen regions) in the bake output metadata
hand the baked texture back to the material pipeline as the projected albedo input
limitations: this script performs no image sampling, projection math, or UV rasterization
camera accuracy is inherited from whatever produced the camera block; an unrefined camera will misalign the projection
unseen-region inference is a heuristic guess, not observed geometry or texture
the resulting bake still needs a rendered overlay review against the reference image before being trusted
projectedTextureBake.note: Feed this descriptor to the Three.js generator/agent to run the actual projection and bake, then re-render and visually compare the baked mesh against the reference image before accepting the result as final.
